## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured N values (10000–10000000) sit past the L2 spill at N≈7598, so the curve starts in the L2-overflow regime. At q=0.01, cost is essentially flat from N=10000 to N=100000 (24.648 → 25.196 ns/p), then rises modestly at N=1000000 (27.246 ns/p) as the working set crosses the L3 spill at N≈243148, and stays flat to N=10000000 (26.687 ns/p). The L3-spill knee is real but small — roughly +2 ns/p. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the N-curve: at q=0.5 the small-N floor is 32.15 ns/p versus 24.648 at q=0.01, and the same mild L3-knee persists (32.15 → 35.282 ns/p). There is no L1d or L2 knee visible because the series begins beyond both.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 2.8 GB/s at N=10000, q=0.01 — only 22% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: frontend stalls dominate at 68.8% even at the smallest N, and compute sits at 31.2%. Bandwidth falls with both N and death rate, reaching 1.96 GB/s (15% of ceiling) at N=1000000, q=0.5, where backend stalls rise to 2.7% and compute drops to 30.0%. At q=0.1 and N≥1000000, backend stalls climb to 9.5–11.3% and compute collapses to 16–18%, marking a transition where churn-driven respawn cost erodes what little throughput existed. The algo never enters a bandwidth-bound regime.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize across particles. The main loop at 0x107f6b9 processes one particle per iteration with a 0x44-byte (68-byte) stride, using scalar `vmovss`/`vmulss`/`vaddss` for per-component math and only incidental packed ops (`vmulps`, `vaddps`, `vmovups`) that operate on components within a single particle. There is no gather and no multi-particle SIMD. The histogram confirms zero vector-suffixed instructions in the NEON sense; the 148 `mov` and 64 `cmp` instructions reflect heavy scalar bookkeeping. The spawn-scan at 0x107fc1e uses `vmovdqu`/`vptest` to bulk-test 32 mask bytes, then unrolls 32 individual `cmp`/`je`/`call` sequences — a 500+ instruction footprint that explains the persistent 68–72% frontend stall. The component-wise packed ops on stride-68 data explain why bandwidth stays low: the core issues too few useful loads per cycle to saturate memory, and the byte-granular mask scatter (`mov BYTE PTR [rsi+r14*1]`) in the respawn path further caps throughput.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01 the algo sustains only 2.8 GB/s = 22% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling, with 68.8% frontend stalls and zero cross-particle vectorization. The compiler produced component-wise packed ops (`vmulps`, `vaddps`) within a single-particle loop body, not the across-particle SIMD the hypothesis requires, and the 619-instruction footprint with a 32-way unrolled spawn scan keeps the frontend saturated. The hypothesis fails even in the death-free regime.
